title: Intrinsic cotangent complex: lci models, Tor-independent base change and smooth specialization
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Write $L_{X/S}\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] for the cotangent complex: on affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ it is the sheafification of the normalized complex of $\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$, placed in nonpositive cohomological degrees, where $P_\bullet\to B$ is the standard simplicial free polynomial $A$-algebra resolution; differentials mean Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. These affine complexes have canonical comparison isomorphisms with the intrinsic complex, compatible with restriction to smaller affine charts. Suppose $U\subset X$ factors as a closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow P$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] into an open of $\mathbf A^n_S$, whose ideal $I$ is locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Then the natural conormal-differential map gives a canonical isomorphism $[I/I^2\xrightarrow{d}i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}]\simeq L_{X/S}|_U$ in degrees $-1,0$, where $i^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. In particular $L_{X/S}|_U$ is perfect of Tor amplitude $[-1,0]$: locally it is a two-term complex of finite locally free modules [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in these degrees. For a Cartesian square $X'=X\times_SS'$, with $g:X'\to X$, which is Tor-independent (on affine charts $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\simeq B\otimes_AA'$), the natural map $Lg^*L_{X/S}\to L_{X'/S'}$ is an isomorphism. Here $Lg^*$ is pullback computed using flat resolutions before tensoring. These natural maps respect identities, composition of base changes and the local conormal models. If $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the canonical map $L_{X/S}\to\Omega^1_{X/S}[0]$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Define the intrinsic complex on $X$ by the free sheaf-algebra resolution of $f^{-1}\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal O_X$ in [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison]. The natural equivalence [lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence] identifies alternating-face and normalized conventions, reindexed by $n\mapsto-n$. On $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ over $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the section maps of the first cited node, composed with $A\to(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S)(U)$, give a map on sections; the adjunction in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], applied degreewise and naturally to the differentials, gives the canonical map $\widetilde L_{B/A}\to L_{X/S}|_U$. At $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}B$, put $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p\cap A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], its stalk is the localization comparison $L_{B/A}\otimes_B B_{\mathfrak p}\to L_{B_{\mathfrak p}/A_{\mathfrak q}}$, hence a quasi-isomorphism by that node. Exactness is detected stalkwise by [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-exact-iff-stalk-exact], applied to the cone. Thus this map is an isomorphism. The section maps already commute with restrictions, so the comparisons agree after every smaller affine restriction; no gluing of arbitrary derived objects is being assumed.

source.place: Tags 08SS, 08SX, 08T0, 08SF; Tag 08T3 (lemma-morphism-affine-schemes), with simplicial.tex Tags 019A/019C. Schemes Tags 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions) and 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), item (7).

proof.text: Work locally on the given immersion over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$, taking a principal affine open of the ambient affine space. Its ring is a localization $P$ of $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and $B=P/I$ with $I$ generated by the specified finite Koszul-regular sequence. The triangle of [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle] has outer terms $L_{P/A}\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}B$ and $L_{B/P}$. By [lem-trf-smooth-cotangent-identification], the first is $(\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_P B)[0]$, using the free differential basis in [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], its localization [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], and the K-flat computation of [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. By [lem-trf-koszul-quotient-cotangent-vanishing], the second is $(I/I^2)[1]$. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] therefore gives $H^j(L_{B/A})=0$ outside $\{-1,0\}$. This supplies the full vanishing that a naive truncation alone cannot give.

Apply [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model] with its kernel $J=I$: the canonical map $L_{B/A}\to[I/I^2\to\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_P B]$ identifies the latter with $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{B/A}$. The vanishing established in Step 2 makes this a quasi-isomorphism of the full complex. Its inverse in $D(B)$ is the stated conormal-model isomorphism. By [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis], the $r$ conormal classes of the equations form a basis of $I/I^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], the other term has basis $\mathrm dx_1,\ldots,\mathrm dx_n$. The comparison is natural under localization by the naive comparison and the intrinsic affine comparison of Step 1; thus these local models describe $L_{X/S}|_U$.

source.place: Tag 08RB (lemma-relation-with-naive-cotangent-complex), Tag 08SL; conormal freeness: more-algebra.tex Tags 0CEM/062I.

proof.text: Each local conormal model is a complex of finite free modules supported in degrees $-1,0$, hence is perfect by the stated local-model definition. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Therefore [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes its derived tensor with a module in degree zero by ordinary tensor with that module. The resulting complex still has zero terms outside $-1,0$, proving the asserted Tor-amplitude bound, also for arbitrary module sheaves after restriction to these opens.

For an affine base-change square put $B'=B\otimes_A A'$ and take the standard polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to B$. By [lem-trf-tor-independent-cotangent-base-change], the hypothesis $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\simeq B'[0]$ makes $P_\bullet\otimes_A A'\to B'$ a polynomial resolution. Let $K=s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B)$. Every term is a free $B$-module on the polynomial differentials by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables]. Thus $K$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'$ by $K\otimes_B B'$. Degreewise the universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] identifies $\Omega^1_{(P_n\otimes_A A')/A'}$ with $\Omega^1_{P_n/A}\otimes_A A'$: both represent $A'$-derivations out of $P_n\otimes_A A'$, by $\mathrm d(p\otimes a')\mapsto\mathrm dp\otimes a'$. These maps commute with the faces. Hence $K\otimes_B B'$ is the differential complex of the tensor resolution, canonically identified with $L_{B'/A'}$ by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Its compatibility with standard functoriality shows this is the natural base-change arrow.

proof.text: The formula in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] computes $Lg^*$ by pulling back a flat-term K-flat representative. On an affine chart, the complex $\widetilde K$ from Step 5 has free sheaf terms and is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]; its module pullback is the sheaf associated to $K\otimes_B B'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change], applied termwise. By Step 5 its comparison to $L_{X'/S'}$ is an isomorphism. The intrinsic comparisons of Step 1 and the section-map naturality in [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison] identify these maps on all restrictions. They therefore prove the asserted global isomorphism $Lg^*L_{X/S}\to L_{X'/S'}$.

source.place: Tag 08QQ with Tags 08SX/08T3; K-flat computation of ringed-space pullback, sites-cohomology.tex section-derived-pullback. Schemes Tag 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), part (1).

proof.text: The standard resolution maps of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] exist for every ring square and preserve identities and composition. Its comparisons for nonstandard polynomial resolutions are natural for their morphisms, so this also applies when the intermediate resolution is the tensor resolution of Step 5. The rebracketing $(K\otimes_B B')\otimes_{B'}B''\cong K\otimes_B B''$ identifies the chain maps for two successive base changes with that for the composite: both send $\mathrm dp\otimes b$ to its image differential times the image of $b$. After the K-flat computation of Steps 5–6, these are the identity and composition laws for the derived comparison maps. Restriction is a special case of the same naturality.

To check compatibility with a conormal model under the same Tor-independent base change, use the local presentation $A\to P\twoheadrightarrow B$ of Step 2 and its Koszul complex $K_P(f)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. This complex resolves $B$. The polynomial algebra is free as an $A$-module on monomials, and [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness] makes its localization $P$ flat over $A$. The bounded Koszul complex therefore has $A$-flat terms and is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], its tensor with $A'$ computes $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\simeq B'$. By [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso], this tensor is $K_{P'}(f')$, where $P'=P\otimes_A A'$. Thus $f'$ is Koszul-regular and $P'/(f')=B'$, so $I'=(f')$ is the kernel. The bases in [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis] on both sides identify the canonical map $(I/I^2)\otimes_B B'\to I'/I'^2$, $[f_i]\otimes1\mapsto[f'_i]$, with the identity matrix; hence it is an isomorphism. This proves conormal base change without assuming that arbitrary tensoring preserves an exact sequence.

source.place: Proof of Tag 08SL and the Koszul base-change argument in Tag 08SJ; more-algebra.tex definition-koszul-regular.

proof.text: In degree zero the differential base-change isomorphism of Step 5 identifies $(\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_P B)\otimes_B B'$ with $\Omega^1_{P'/A'}\otimes_{P'}B'$. Together with Step 8 this identifies the tensor of the conormal complex with the base-changed conormal complex. The differentials agree because $\mathrm d(f'_i)$ is the image of $\mathrm df_i$. Apply the naturality square of [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model] to the supplied square of presentations $P\to P'$, $B\to B'$. Both conormal complexes are K-flat two-term models by Step 4, and both comparison maps from the full cotangent complexes are isomorphisms by Steps 2–3. Inverting these maps gives precisely the compatibility of the natural base-change isomorphism with the conormal models. This argument also covers localization and any supplied morphism of presentations.

source.place: Tag 08RB and the explicit comparison of Tag 08UP; functoriality Tag 08QL.

proof.text: If $f$ is smooth, [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] gives affine neighbourhoods with $A\to P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\to B$, where $P\to B$ is etale. The triangle [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle], its long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], and the full vanishing $L_{B/P}=0$ from [lem-trf-etale-cotangent-vanishing] identify $L_{B/A}$ with $L_{P/A}\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}B$. By [lem-trf-smooth-cotangent-identification], this is $(\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_P B)[0]$, so all nonzero-degree cohomology vanishes. The naive comparison [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model], applied to a polynomial surjection onto $B$, identifies $H^0(L_{B/A})$ with the cokernel of the conormal differential. That cokernel is $\Omega^1_{B/A}$: by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], derivations from the polynomial algebra factor through $B$ exactly when they kill the relations. Thus the canonical augmentation $L_{B/A}\to\Omega^1_{B/A}[0]$ is an isomorphism. These canonical augmentations commute with restrictions by [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison], hence prove $L_{X/S}\simeq\Omega^1_{X/S}[0]$ globally. The etale factor is essential; no assertion that a smooth morphism is locally a polynomial algebra is used.
